# Conclave

> Conclave is a self-hosted agent harness and hub. It runs coding agents with any model on your own computers, checks their work before a turn ends, and lets you steer them from a web app, desktop app, terminal app or phone. You run the hub yourself (Docker, Proxmox LXC, Linux, macOS, or inside the desktop app). There is no Conclave cloud; model calls go straight to the provider you pick. License: AGPL-3.0-only. Written in TypeScript on Bun with one SQLite file; Android app in Kotlin; desktop app in Tauri.

## What it is

- A hub (`conclave serve`) that holds the agent loop, chats, memory, routines, usage and keys.
- Device programs on PCs and Macs that connect out to the hub over a WebSocket, so no inbound ports are needed. Each session picks the device its tools run on.
- Clients: web app, desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux), native Android app, iPhone home screen app, terminal app.

## Features

- Native harness built from Claude Code's public design: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, Task, TodoWrite, AskUserQuestion and Skill tools, permission rules, hooks, skills, subagents, auto-compaction and prompt caching. Works with any model.
- Verify gate: after a turn that edited files, the project's check runs on the session's device before the turn may end; a failure sends the agent back with the last 40 lines, up to 3 times per user turn.
- Multi-model chat: second opinion on any message, jury (juror names can be hidden from the judge), debate, model switch, and loop until a command passes.
- Vendor harnesses over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP): Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode run as engines and share one transcript with native turns. Their permission prompts become Conclave approvals.
- Usage limits: failover to your next plan or key for the same model in your account order, then to the next model on a Usage fallback list; long waits pause the session and resume it when the limit resets.
- Subscriptions through CLIProxyAPI, which the hub runs: Claude, ChatGPT, Google, Grok, Kimi and Muse plans. Also API keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, GLM (Z.ai), DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio and any OpenAI-compatible API.
- File conflict warnings when two live sessions write the same file; stuck alerts when a turn makes no progress.
- Workflows: scripts in Claude Code's workflow API, run in QuickJS compiled to WebAssembly with no file system, process or network, and a journal that lets a run resume and replay finished calls.
- Approvals from the phone (Android app and Web Push with Allow and Deny).
- Several people on one hub, each with their own accounts, chats, memory, keys, devices and budgets.
- Shared long-term memory across models and devices, with a Basic Memory adapter.
- Routines on a schedule; missed runs catch up after downtime.
- ShareFile: agents hand back files (PDF, images, spreadsheets, zip) as file cards with download.
- Automatic updates installed when nothing is running.
- Permission rules, a dangerous-command guard, checkpoints you can undo and an audit log. No OS sandbox for commands yet.
